headline: The AI blog Kingy AI says StepFun has put the weights of its 600-billion-parameter Step 5 Preview model online, under a licence with conditions for large commercial users.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: a real open-weight release, but verified only by file listings and the licence, with no model test.
importance_line: Researchers and companies with large GPU clusters can now study or host a big open-weight model from China's StepFun, but ordinary machines cannot run it, the licence adds duties for big commercial users, and nobody has tested its quality.
summary: Kingy AI reports that StepFun, a Chinese AI developer, has made the weights of Step 5 Preview public, a mixture-of-experts model with 600 billion parameters in total and 27 billion in use at a time, with a 394 GB version in NVFP4 (a compressed number format) and a 650 GB FP8 version. The blog read the files and the StepFun Model License 1.0, which allows use and redistribution but adds attribution and commercial-agreement duties above set user or revenue levels, and says it has not run the model or confirmed when the files first went public.
notes: Kingy AI checked the repositories itself on 14 Oct 2026; StepFun's own model card is its source for the parameter counts. Publication date of the release unverified.
